comments.text: 2026-07-16 VK image-hotpath audit found and fixed a real bypass: the three-pod oracle previously inspected cache state but never authenticated created/rotated/deleted secrets, allowing /v1/models to return 200 for a rotated secret. The handler now resolves supplied VKs from the governance pod-local authority cache, rejects missing/inactive/revoked keys with 401, and honors the bounded freshness lease with 503 instead of doing a per-request DB lookup. The strengthened k3s/local-Aurora oracle now proves create accepted on all 3 pods, old secret rejected after rotate, new secret accepted, deleted secret rejected, restart replay, and inference+MCP stale-close after Postgres partition. Full loose-binary 3-node run passed. Next required proof is the same oracle against the immutable published v0.3.4 image digest.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: 2026-07-16 strengthened serving-path audit exposed a second, broader VK bypass: on ordinary /v1/chat/completions, provider queue lookup ran before GovernancePlugin.PreLLMHook, so an old rotated secret reached provider discovery and returned 400 provider-not-configured instead of the authority 401. Strict TDD reproduced the ordering defect for both non-streaming and streaming requests. Commit bd593033f moves provider discovery after plugin short-circuit and post-routing identity in both paths. Full core tests, targeted race tests, vet, and the local three-node oracle passed; the oracle now proves rotated/deleted rejection on both list-models and chat plus list-models/chat/MCP stale-close after the PostgreSQL authority partition. Immutable released-image proof remains required before closing.

title: Prove RDS Proxy and direct PostgreSQL listener topology
description:
Build an executable oracle for Aurora PostgreSQL outbox wakeups across the launch listener topology: app traffic may use RDS Proxy/pooling, but durable outbox authority remains PostgreSQL and LISTEN/NOTIFY is only a wakeup hint.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- A test harness runs one durable polling consumer plus the chosen listener path through Aurora writer failover and RDS Proxy interruption; every committed outbox row at or below the final watermark is applied exactly once or explicitly deduplicated by revision.
- The harness proves a direct listener reconnect gap cannot lose correctness because cursor polling catches all missed rows.
- The harness proves notifications delivered through an unsupported transaction-pooled path are not required for correctness and cannot be the only delivery mechanism.
- Duplicate, reordered, and missing notifications advance no local snapshot past the durable cursor and do not revive stale policy.
- Metrics expose listener reconnect count, poll catch-up lag, last applied revision, and stale-closed duration.

title: Prove optional Redis acceleration cannot become authority
description:
Define and test the optional Redis accelerator contract for horizontal scaling. Redis may reduce latency or fanout, but launch correctness must remain on Aurora/PostgreSQL authority, reservations, and outbox replay when Redis is absent or lost.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- The same governance/config/MCP freshness suite passes with Redis disabled, Redis enabled, Redis flushed, Redis partitioned, and Redis restarted mid-stream.
- Redis loss never extends a revoked key, stale authorization epoch, exhausted reservation, disabled MCP grant, or reduced routing policy beyond the signed freshness lease.
- Redis-stored hints are either rebuilt from Aurora/outbox/bootstrap snapshots or ignored fail-closed; no Redis value is accepted without a durable revision/epoch check.
- Metrics distinguish accelerator hit/miss/loss from authoritative freshness and reservation decisions.
- Documentation names Redis as non-mandatory for Kubernetes launch and lists the exact features that may use it only as an accelerator.

title: Prove authority leases under clock skew
description:
Build deterministic tests for freshness leases, authorization epochs, outbox cursors, and reservation expiry under pod, node, and database clock skew. The oracle must prove launch behavior uses monotonic revisions and database/lease authority rather than trusting local pod wall clocks.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- With pod clocks skewed forward and backward beyond the freshness lease, revoked keys, removed groups, reduced budgets, disabled MCP grants, and reduced routing policies fail stale-closed by logical revision/epoch and cannot be prolonged by local time.
- Reservation expiry and renewal tests use a single authoritative time source or fenced compare-and-swap state; stale renewals cannot revive abandoned reservations.
- Outbox application order remains revision/watermark based when event timestamps are equal, reversed, or skewed.
- Kubernetes readiness/startup refuses protected traffic before an initial signed snapshot regardless of local clock.
- Metrics expose clock-skew suspicion separately from ordinary outbox lag or DB outage.

title: Prove 100-pod bootstrap backpressure and notification storms
description:
Build the horizontal-scaling acceptance oracle that goes beyond the three-pod conformance suite: 100 stateless pods cold-start, catch up from Aurora/PostgreSQL authority, and survive notification storms without making Redis mandatory.

Acceptance / failure oracles:
- A 100-pod test boots from empty local state against a bounded Aurora/outbox backlog; pods do not accept protected requests until an initial signed snapshot and required cursors are installed.
- Notification storms, reordered wakeups, and dropped wakeups cannot create duplicate application, cursor regression, stale policy revival, or DB thundering herd beyond configured backpressure limits.
- Backpressure protects Aurora by bounding concurrent bootstrap readers, LISTEN reconnects, snapshot downloads, and per-tenant catch-up work while preserving starvation-free progress.
- Pod, node, and zone loss during bootstrap/recovery leaves surviving pods available within the documented stale-closed rules and lets replacement pods converge from durable state.
- The report records actual lag, queue depth, retry, WAL/autovacuum, and CPU/memory data without inventing benchmark thresholds before measurement.

This is analytics design and governed evidence work only; it must not become employee surveillance, individual performance ranking, content collection by default, or a new inference hot-path dependency. Reuse the canonical evidence envelope and sanitized-copy boundaries; preserve tenant, purpose, region, retention, deletion, consent, and minimum-cohort policy. title: Implement privacy-preserving aggregation and access controls
description: Design aggregate query/materialization contracts with minimum cohorts, k-anonymity or equivalent cell suppression, differential query budgets where needed, complementary-cell and repeated-query resistance, role/purpose checks, subject-access export, deletion propagation, and metadata-only behavior when consent or transform policy is absent. No manager ranking, employment decisions, or inferred protected/emotional traits.

Define backpressure, loss accounting, idempotency, clock skew, schema evolution, and disabled-consumer behavior; prove inference latency is unaffected and raw content/credentials never escape.

Suggestions must include evidence window, cohort/sample size, uncertainty, privacy receipt, explanation, human approval state, and rollback/expiry. Define a governance-first overview with team and user dimensions visible at a glance, direct labels, sparse trend lines/sparklines, explicit compared-to baseline, and no decorative chart controls. Specify source, timestamp, sample size, empty/loading/error states, RBAC behavior, accessibility, and which unfinished capabilities are hidden. Deliver a self-contained IA spec plus chart-by-chart acceptance criteria and Playwright selectors. Tufte gates: lie factor approximately 1, maximum data-ink, no redundant legends/labels, direct labeling, micro plus macro views.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: Planning review via tufte-viz: charts must answer compared-to-what, use direct labels, preserve source/time/sample metadata, and pass lie-factor/data-ink/empty-state gates. This is intentionally a design bead before implementation.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: 2026-07-16: first implementation slice landed: dashboard defaults to governance team rankings and time-series charts default to low-ink line views (URL overrides preserved). title: Implement team and user dashboard default views
description: Implement the approved IA so the dashboard defaults to enterprise governance views: team spend/requests/latency and user spend/requests/limits, with shared time/filter state and drill-through to logs. Preserve virtual-key and provider breakdowns as secondary views. Reconcile every displayed value to API responses; capability-hide unavailable data; add unit tests and Playwright critical-flow coverage for RBAC, empty state, filters, and direct links.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: JSM-style implementation gate: no chart is complete unless API values reconcile, RBAC hides unauthorized dimensions, shared filters/deep links work, and Playwright covers team/user default, empty, loading, error, and drill-through states.

title: Add governance dashboard data contract and provenance metadata
description: Define stable API/read-model contracts for team/user request volume, cost, token usage, latency, error/overdraft counts, limits and freshness. Every series carries source, generated_at, window, sample size, aggregation and reconciliation status. Prevent unsupported region/provider claims and distinguish missing cost from zero. Add contract fixtures and API tests.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: Provenance requirement: dashboard read models must distinguish zero from missing, expose freshness and reconciliation status, and prevent unsupported region/provider claims. This is the contract foundation for the Tufte IA.

title: Complete overdraft alert delivery adapters and audit trail
description: Build on the OverdraftNotifier seam. Specify and implement adapters for SNS/SQS, webhook and in-product notifications without putting provider clients in the request hot path. Define retries, idempotency keys, dead-letter behavior, PII minimization, user/team routing, approval/breach/expiry events, metrics and audit records. Add fake-adapter conformance tests and document AWS SNS integration.

comments.author: pierre
comments.text: Notification design must remain async and transport-agnostic. SNS/SQS are adapters, not hot-path dependencies; every event needs idempotency, retry/DLQ, PII minimization, audit, and user/team routing.

title: Add Okta SSO login and session governance to the web dashboard
description: Provide first-class Okta OIDC login for the FrankenGate dashboard. Define issuer/client/audience validation, PKCE and state/nonce handling, redirect allowlists, session cookie rotation and logout, group-to-role mapping, tenant/team/user scoping, RBAC enforcement on every dashboard/API route, fail-closed behavior when identity claims are stale, and local-development fallback without weakening production. Acceptance: Playwright covers login, callback failure, logout, expired session, group membership changes, unauthorized deep links, CSRF/state replay, and audit events; no access token or provider secret is exposed to browser storage or logs; docs include Okta setup and claim mapping.

title: Implement Okta OIDC login UI and callback handoff
description: Build the dashboard's easy-login experience around Okta OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE. Add a login entry point, loading/error states, callback handoff, session bootstrap, logout, and unauthorized/deep-link handling. Keep tokens out of localStorage/sessionStorage and browser logs; use secure HttpOnly SameSite cookies issued by the backend. Preserve a clearly isolated local-development fallback that cannot be enabled in production. Acceptance: Playwright covers login success, provider denial, state/nonce mismatch, expired session, logout, unauthorized deep link, keyboard accessibility, and mobile viewport; API/client types remain generated or explicitly typed; no provider secret or access token is rendered in the UI.

title: Implement Okta session, claims, and dashboard RBAC enforcement
description: Implement the backend OIDC session boundary for the web dashboard: issuer/discovery validation, client/audience checks, PKCE state and nonce verification, redirect allowlist, secure rotating session cookies, logout/revocation behavior, JWKS/key rotation handling, group-to-role mapping, team/user scoping, and fail-closed behavior for stale or malformed claims. Enforce authorization on every dashboard API and page route rather than trusting UI visibility. Emit audit events for login, logout, callback failure, denied access, group/role changes, and session expiry. Acceptance: unit tests cover signature/issuer/audience/nonce/state/expiry/key-rotation failures and role boundaries; integration tests prove protected routes cannot be bypassed by direct requests; secrets/tokens are absent from logs.

title: Document Okta dashboard setup and provide operator verification
description: Document the Okta application setup required for the FrankenGate dashboard: redirect/logout URIs, issuer and audience configuration, PKCE requirements, required claims, group-to-role mapping, team scoping, cookie/proxy considerations, local development mode, and incident recovery for signing-key or group changes. Add a deterministic operator verification checklist and configuration validation/doctor output that detects missing or unsafe settings before production startup. Acceptance: docs match the actual config schema and routes; examples contain no real secrets; a smoke test validates the configured discovery endpoint and claim mapping without logging credentials.
